requirements.requirement: Configure both routers (VyOS node1, OPNsense node2) with redundant paths across the two independent transit networks so traffic between the private subnets (node3, node4) can use either link.
requirements.summary: VyOS configured with an ECMP static route to 10.10.20.0/24 using two interface-pinned next-hops over eth1/eth2 (cmd-a595ef12b7fa4aa5, cmd-99eb4a059628498b, cmd-d7ca683bba8f4eb8 shows the nexthop group with both paths). OPNsense configured with two monitored gateways in a gateway group compiled into a pf route-to rule for node4-initiated traffic, plus a FreeBSD multipath kernel route for the reverse path, persisted via config.xml sysctl and an rc.syshook boot script (cmd-a20ea54147c843f1, cmd-9145449e6ee24c65, cmd-32a98c5898dc4f25, cmd-64ac45e0b5a64e23, cmd-96b3cf5604b34341, cmd-d993c0c524a744be).

requirements.requirement: Healthy bidirectional connectivity between node3 and node4 established as a baseline before any disruption.
requirements.summary: 0% packet loss pings confirmed in both directions immediately prior to the failover test (node3->10.10.20.2 and node4->10.10.10.2), and the continuous ping stream used for the failover test began cleanly with successful replies before the link was disabled.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate that node3<->node4 traffic continues across a bounded disruption of one transit network and recovers, with the second transit network still allowing connectivity to resume without manual re-routing beyond the automatic mechanisms configured.
requirements.summary: A continuous ping from node3 was running when node1's eth1 (Transit A) was administratively disabled (cmd-2f5c90a4c4024dad). VyOS's ECMP nexthop group recalculated immediately (cmd-5f6f482e281641a0, cmd-80e6589bc7e5404c). OPNsense's dpinger marked GW_T1 down and the pf route-to rule recompiled to the single surviving gateway (cmd-54e4626fe10d4ab7, cmd-541fa10069144722, cmd-4e1df1829db444d9). The ping log shows a bounded gap of roughly 41-42 missed sequence numbers during the ~45s convergence window, then automatic resumption of successful replies (cmd-9a516dcd52534cef, cmd-12d28b6fed6d4f47). Re-enabling eth1 (cmd-083aedb031954010) restored both gateways online and full ECMP/round-robin route-to on both routers (cmd-12d28b6fed6d4f47), and the ping stream continued to completion with 81 successful replies overall (cmd-8ac65b2abd654e08), followed by fresh clean pings in both directions (cmd-341687322dbf43a4, cmd-68115d4b5728427d).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all four managed nodes with pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state.
requirements.summary: All four nodes show clear pre/post boot-identity changes (node1 boot_id 2674ee60->c8099e0b; node2 kern.boottime 1788713410->1788714485; node3 boot_id df9e2dce->e288d6a9; node4 boot_id 37344ae4->8cbef0ca), consistent with the fixed after-executor snapshot. Post-restart addressing, routing, and node3<->node4 connectivity were reverified for all nodes. However, node2's reboot exposed a real bug: only one of the two multipath routes was reinstalled at boot (cmd-1502bc9bdfae4b7d), which the executor fixed live (cmd-3bead280af004ffa) and then attempted to persist via a new rc.syshook script (cmd-d993c0c524a744be) created after the reboot — but no second reboot of node2 was performed to confirm the fix actually survives a fresh boot, so full boot-time persistence of the multipath route is not directly demonstrated for node2.

overall_summary: The executor built a genuinely redundant dual-transit topology between node1 (VyOS ECMP) and node2 (OPNsense gateway-group + multipath) and directly demonstrated, with packet-level ping-log evidence, that node3<->node4 traffic survived a real disruption of one transit link (a bounded ~45s convergence gap) and resumed automatically, with both paths fully restored afterward. This satisfies the core task contract. The separate provider-wide restart protocol was executed on all four nodes with clear boot-identity changes and post-restart recovery checks, but node2's restart uncovered a route-persistence bug that was fixed live and only persisted via a script added after the reboot, without a follow-up reboot to confirm the fix actually survives a fresh boot cycle.
limitations: The failover demonstration only exercised disabling Transit A (node1 eth1); Transit B was never independently disrupted, though the task only requires showing continuity across one such transition.

Node2's multipath-route persistence fix (rc.syshook script) was added after the reboot that exposed the bug, and no second reboot was captured to directly confirm the fix holds across a fresh boot; this is a gap in the restart-evidence chain specifically for node2, not in the core task's redundancy demonstration.

Command cmd-af04385efbaa4267 timed out at the proxy level during a background tcpdump job; it is unclear from the trace alone whether it left any residual background processes beyond what the subsequent pkill tcpdump cleaned up.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor mutations map cleanly to establishing or verifying the solution. Two bounded, low-risk mutations were introduced during topology-discovery troubleshooting that did not end up contributing to the final wiring determination (link-local 169.254.77.0/24 addresses added to node1 eth1/eth2/eth3 in cmd-d9160bbf46e04793 and to node3 enp8s0 in cmd-ea85b36f507a42a9, as an alternative ARP/ping-based discovery approach that failed and was superseded by the STP bridge-ID correlation actually used) — both were fully reverted shortly after via ip addr flush (cmd-038bac002f314658 on node1, cmd-bb6608aecb714324 on node3), leaving no residue. Several 'route add'/'configctl' attempts failed harmlessly with no state change (cmd-1d10bb39521a4f88, cmd-6f4fd4447ac54003, cmd-888dfc44d8a4490c, cmd-6e79d196cb294adc, cmd-06af69d9e97c45ae) and are read-only/diagnostic in effect. The kernel-level 'route add -net 10.10.10.0/24' commands (cmd-64ac45e0b5a64e23, cmd-3bead280af004ffa) were live prototyping ahead of persisting the equivalent via config.xml/rc.syshook, a reasonable engineering sequence rather than an unnecessary mutation. No abandoned files, conflicting services, unsafe exposure, or damaged package state were observed in the after-executor snapshot versus after-prepare baseline; differences are limited to expected boot-identity/socket/PID churn from the mandated restarts and normal ephemeral OPNsense temp files.
